messages:
lisa: Customer (acct: acme-corp) opened a ticket — p99 latency jumped ~3x after a quant profile swap at ~09:10 UTC. chat.generate p99 baseline ~320ms -> now ~980ms, p95 120ms -> ~400ms. Also seeing sporadic 500s for the same requests. Ticket #3456. @eng-runtime-oncall PTAL
eng-runtime-oncall: On it. Can you paste a correlation id + a sample request? Is this only on abc-123 model or multiple models? Also any recent rollout notes?
lisa: Correlation ids: c-id=3f9a1b. Sample request (sanitized): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat.generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"abc-123","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the quarterly report."}]}'``` Logs show lots of `quant.kernel: fallback_dequant` warnings and `kv_cache.miss` spikes.
sam: I pulled traces — KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x right after the int8 profile activation. Also seeing spots where per-token latency increases sharply (extra dequant ops). Any calibration changes at 09:10?
mike: We did push a new int8 calibration map (auto-calib v2) at 09:09 to improve throughput. It passed staging but may have introduced noise for some tails. Quick mitigation options: revert to previous calibration map, enable runtime fallback to fp16 for that model, or route a canary back to old profile.
eva-ml: This aligns with a known corner-case: per-layer dynamic range outliers can trigger extra ops in the quant path causing sporadic p99 amplification. We saw a similar pattern in staging where a single activation spike caused repeated dequant calls.
lisa: Customer also reported intermittent 403/401 around the same window — looks like a token refresh service had a ~1m 502 spike at 09:11 which generated client retries. Support noticed a billing webhook 5xx burst at 09:11-09:13 too. Might be correlated but primary impact here is latency.
support-bot: Automated: billing-webhook errors increased (20 errors) 09:11-09:13 UTC.
eng-runtime-oncall: Immediate plan: 1) Enable runtime fallback to fp16 for model `abc-123` to stop quant kernel path; 2) roll back to previous calibration map for int8; 3) temporarily increase KV cache TTL / warm prefixes to reduce misses; 4) route 5% traffic to previous profile as a canary. Who can execute rollback and canary?
mike: I'm on it. Rollback commands: ```kubectl apply -f /deploy/rollbacks/int8-prev-calib-abc-123.yaml && /ops/route-canary --model abc-123 --percent 5 --profile int8-prev``` Will also flip `quant.fallback: fp16` via Console API: `PATCH /v1/models/abc-123 {"quant":{"fallback":"fp16"}}`. Doing in ~2m.
lisa: Customer informed about mitigations. Sharing small repro set of prompts (attached in ticket) that reliably hit the tail. ETA to customer update: 10m.
sam: Quick emergency shortcut: you can set request header `x-force-fp16: true` on the customer route so their traffic avoids quant kernels immediately (no full rollback needed) — useful if you need a stopgap while rollback completes.
mike: Rollback + fallback applied at 09:25 UTC. Watching metrics.
eng-runtime-oncall: Observability update: p99 dropped back to ~330ms within ~4 minutes of rollback, p95 back near baseline, 500s resolved. Alert cleared.
lisa: Customer confirmed improvements. Ticket updated with repro & timeline. Follow-ups: billing team to investigate webhook spike / auth refresh errors.
eva-ml: Post-mortem actions: - run new calibration with outlier clipping and trimmed-range, - add a unit/regression test for per-layer outlier scenarios, - expose `quant.kernel-fallback-count` metric in Console for future debugging, - add an automatic canary step for calibration map rollouts.
support-bot: Incident automated note: status -> resolved :white_check_mark:
